evan: Quick heads-up — saw OOMs on canary for model-x (gpt-like, 16B) when bursty traffic pushed batch 6->8 at seq=2048. allocator failure at FlashAttention workspace allocate.
sophia: ugh. do you have the alloc traces / nvprof snippet?
ev an: pasted below. main culprit is a 3.2GB transient allocation for FA when batch*seq increases, plus KV cache growth for streaming requests.
ev an: ```
[alloc] 2026-02-10 14:08:12.123 alloc_slab: request=3244034560 bytes, free=1200450560 bytes -> fail
[stack] runtime::flash_attention::alloc_workspace(+0x1a)
[alloc] 2026-02-10 14:08:12.124 kv_cache: grow_by=256MB, total_kv=1.6GB
[context] batch=8, seq_len=2048, head_dim=128, n_heads=32
```
sophia: thanks. so two pressure sources: FA workspace and per-request KV. nice catch.
raj: quick thought — we should avoid monolithic per-kernel allocs for FA at high batch. consider split-workspace or per-batch-slice allocation (streaming-friendly). Also fragmentation from many small reserves is making the slab unusable.
clare: profiling shows Triton-attn kernels used less peak memory in similar runs but were 12% slower in throughput for short seq. cuBLASLt path is more stable but suboptimal for attention math. Which heuristic are we using currently in kernel-chooser?
ev an: chooser currently: prefer FlashAttention if seq<=4096 and head_dim % 32==0 and batch<=6 else fallback to Triton/CuBLASLt. That batch<=6 is our legacy cap — canaries pushed it over.
sophia: can we change chooser to be memory-aware rather than only based on seq/batch thresholds? i.e., estimate workspace_per_sample and multiply by requested batch + active_kv(bytes) and compare to slab_free - safety_margin.
raj: yes — propose heuristics: workspace_est = kernel_table[(kernel, seq, head_dim)] * batch; kv_est = avg_kv_per_stream * active_streams; if workspace_est + kv_est > slab_free * 0.8 -> pick an alternative with lower mem footprint or run batch_split.
clare: we have some profiling numbers in /opt/perf/artifacts: FA_workspace_per_sample ~ 52KB for seq512 but scales superlinearly with seq beyond 1024 due to internal tiling. Observed values: seq=512 -> 52KB, seq=1024 -> 220KB, seq=2048 -> 390KB. That explains the 3.2GB at batch 8.
ev an: exactly. current chooser assumes linear scaling which is wrong. need table driven and monotonic backoff.
perf-bot: Perf regression alert: master@a1b2c3 introduced allocator changes (PR #832) that changed the slab free threshold default from 0.75->0.65 on 2026-01-28. Affected runs: model-x canaries.
sophia: noted — PR changed evict policy too, reducing proactive KV eviction. That combined with bad chooser = OOM window.
raj: short-term mitigation: revert the aggressive slab-min usage change (set back to 0.75), and modify chooser to compute memory_estimate using a small table for FA and Triton. Also add batch_split when memory tight (split batch into 2 slices with re-merge).
clare: batch_split tradeoffs: increases latency slightly but avoids OOM and keeps throughput. We already have batch-slicing in the serving runtime but it's gated off for attention kernels because addon logic wasn't memory-safe. Easy enable with guard.
ev an: I'll open a hotfix PR: 1802-fix-chooser-memory-aware + revert slab-min. Drafting tests: microbench with synthetic bursts (5->10) at seq 2048, track max_alloc and fragmentation ratio.
sophia: add a metric: kernel_workspace_est_vs_actual to console dashboards so we can tune table entries. Also add evaluation that simulates KV-heavy streaming to catch combos.
raj: longer term: implement shared workspace for FlashAttention where the kernel requests subregions instead of one giant block; will reduce fragmentation and enable reuse across concurrent calls. Might need Triton kernel changes.
clare: agree. also investigate using cuBLASLt for the FFN matmul path when attention chooses FA — splitting responsibilities may reduce peaks. FFN currently takes a non-trivial workspace.
ev an: plan and ETA: hotfix PR in next 2 hours, canary tomorrow with reverted slab threshold + chooser memory-aware. Follow-up design doc for shared workspace and kernel API in eng-runtime/notes repo.
sophia: sg. @perf-bot please create a perf run for model-x canary after deploy. :thumbsup:
ev an: thanks — will link PR here when ready.```
